title: Troubleshoot a Bedrock sugar cane farm
summary: Find out whether a sugar cane farm is losing output during growth, harvesting or collection.

body.text: Watch one stalk through a harvest. Check whether it grows, whether the upper cane breaks, and whether the dropped item reaches storage. The first step that fails tells you where to look.

Place a dirt or sand block with water against one of its four sides, at the same height as the planting block. Plant cane on top and leave two blocks of air above it. A water trench can serve a whole row if every planting block touches the trench. Water below the row or diagonally across a corner does not count.

Unaided cane grows in stages to three blocks tall. In Bedrock, bone meal can bring a short stalk to full height. Use it on the control plant when you want to check the layout without waiting for natural growth. Leave the bottom segment in place when harvesting so the plant can grow again.

head: What you see
What to test
rows: Compare the support block and the water level with your control plant.
Watch one cycle in the reference world. Compare the height and facing of the harvesting components at that same stalk in your build.
Cane breaks and the planting spot is empty
Watch which segment breaks first. Check whether the base lost its supporting block or adjacent water during the cycle.
Cane drops but storage stays empty
Drop one cane item at the landing point. Follow it to the first place it stops. Check for a gap, a full container or a hopper facing away from its destination.

body.text: Expand one module at a time

Run the original and the new module from the same player position. Watch the farthest stalk through one harvest and trace its drops to the shared chest. If both modules harvest but only the near one delivers, inspect the connection between the two collection lines before changing the growing area.
TheySix B172 is a stackable design you can open in a separate world to observe a working harvest and collection cycle.
Mechanics reference: Minecraft Wiki, Sugar Cane.
